problem_statement: sem_destroy() returns the wrong result for the EBUSY case. POSIX requires sem_destroy to fail with -1 and errno EBUSY when another thread is currently blocked waiting on the semaphore, and to succeed when no thread is waiting. Instead, the implementation bases the EBUSY decision on the semaphore's count value rather than on whether a thread is actually waiting: it fails to report EBUSY when a thread is blocked but the count is 0, and it would report EBUSY whenever the count is non-zero even if no thread is waiting. After the fix, sem_destroy must return -1 with errno EBUSY while a thread is blocked on sem_wait (regardless of count), and must succeed once that thread has been woken and is no longer waiting.
